d4_arrive: Day four. Hudson's handle. The full sweep returns — same stations, same breath — with the attunement phrase swapped: feel what it is to want, without a subject. One new station near the end is yours: many wants at once, none suppressed. Timers start at zero, as always. Begin when you're ready.
d4_soak1: First — the instruction this course grows from, once more, in his words. The most important of all of them, is to feel wanting. To allow yourself to have the physical, emotional experience of wanting. To just sit in that, to bathe in that, to savor that feeling. And do it without — don't even have a subject at first. Just feel what it is to want.
d4_soak1_verify: Today, that sentence is the practice, verbatim: what it is to want, without a subject.
d4_soak2: Second voice. Hudson, on why the subject matters. We shape our world around our identity, far more than the world shapes us. The wants are the evolutionary path. Evolution means that your identity changes. If there's any reason to feel like it's vulnerable to be in your wants, it's because you will be destroyed, or evolve. You can call it whatever you want to call it, but it's the same thing.
d4_soak2_verify: So — without a subject isn't just technique. The subject is the thing that wanting evolves.
d4_soak3: Third voice. Hudson, on direction. When we follow our desire to walk, as soon as we get there, there's the next desire, that pulls us on that evolutionary path. That's the want — it's telling me to go in that direction. That's all that's necessary.
d4_soak3_verify: A want needs nothing but a direction. No justification. No case to make.
d4_soak4: The last voice is yours, from day one. It's like this felt sense of potential. It has something of the beginning of hunger, the beginning of the sensual. There's a sense of how it feels very connected to action, and to the rest of the world. When everything is imbued with this, there is this kind of magnetism within the stillness. — Three days later: does that description still match what you find? Say what's changed, if anything has.
d4_practice_intro: The sit. The full sweep, with the new handle. Same stations, same breath — only the reaching-for is different: not a quality you attune to, but a verb you feel. Each dwell runs the length you set; the chime is permission, not a demand.
d4_st_ground: Ground. Before the sweep: inhabit your midsection, between your ribs and your pelvis, and rest for a moment on your own power. Yesterday's ground, carried forward. Set this one short — it's a doorstep, not a room.
d4_st_pelvis: Pelvis. Now inhabit your pelvis and genital area. Feel what it is to want, without a subject, within your pelvis and genital area. Bring your breath down into your pelvis, and feel it move through the wanting.
d4_st_midsection: Midsection. Inhabit your midsection, between your ribs and your pelvis. Feel what it is to want, without a subject, within your midsection. Bring your breath down into your midsection, and feel it move through the wanting.
d4_st_chest: Chest. Inhabit your chest. Let yourself settle within your chest, so that you feel that you are sitting in your heart. Feel what it is to want, without a subject, within your chest. This does not need to be a big feeling; just let yourself feel a little of the wanting within your chest. Bring your breath down into your chest, and feel it move through the wanting.
d4_st_neck: Neck. Inhabit your neck. Feel what it is to want, without a subject, within your neck. Bring your breath down into your neck, and let it move through the wanting.
d4_st_head: Head. Inhabit your whole brain. Feel what it is to want, without a subject, within your whole brain. Bring your breath straight back through your head on the inhale, and let it release on the exhale. Feel it move through the wanting.
d4_st_wholebody: Whole body. Now feel that you are in your whole body all at once, including your arms and legs, your whole torso, neck, and head. Feel what it is to want pervading your whole body, so that it feels like you are made of wanting.
d4_st_manywants: Many wants at once. Your station — you built it yesterday, mid-sit. Let several of your current wants arise together. Allow all of them to exist at once, and to move freely through the space — none suppressed because it seems right or wrong for the situation. Subjects will come with them; let them come, and keep feeling the wanting underneath all of it. Nothing to choose today.
d4_st_everything: Everything. Find the space outside your body, the space in the room. Feel that the space inside and outside of your body is the same continuous space. Slowly open your eyes. Without moving at all from within your body, attune to the space — and the wanting — pervading your body and everything in your environment, at the same time. Experience everything as desire. Or, in today's words: everything, wanting.
d4_prompt_manywants: What was it like — all of them at once? Tap, and speak. Or continue.
d4_sayitback: Say it back. Two doors, one room? Blackstone reaches for a quality: the raw quality of desire, before any object. Hudson reaches for a verb: what it is to want, without a subject. In your own words: did the two handles open the same room? What was different, in your body? Tap, and speak, when ready.
d4_sayitback_sources: The handles, side by side. Blackstone's, as this course adapted it: the raw quality of desire — wanting itself, before any object. Hudson's: just feel what it is to want, without a subject. The course keeps her handle as the main text, with his as the variation — today you felt the difference. Whatever you found is data for the build.
d4_close: That's the day. In the field: when several wants collide today, give them ten seconds of coexistence before any choosing — all of them felt, none suppressed. Notice what choosing feels like, after that. Export when you're ready. Day five comes from what you found.
